cross_validation

Yiran Jin

2026-11-16

library(tidyverse)
library(p8105.datasets)
library(modelr)
library(mgcv)
## Loading required package: nlme
## 
## Attaching package: 'nlme'
## The following object is masked from 'package:dplyr':
## 
##     collapse
## This is mgcv 1.9-1. For overview type 'help("mgcv-package")'.

LIDAR data

data("lidar")

lidar_df = 
  lidar |> 
  mutate(id = row_number()) |> 
  select(id, everything())

lidar_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = range, y = logratio)) + 
  geom_point()

Build my training and testing datasets.

train_df = sample_frac(lidar_df, size = .8)
test_df  = anti_join(lidar_df, train_df, by = "id")
ggplot(train_df, aes(x = range, y = logratio)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_point(data = test_df, color = "red")

fit some models

linear_mod = lm(logratio ~ range, data = train_df)
smooth_mod = gam(logratio ~ s(range), data = train_df)
wiggly_mod = gam(logratio ~ s(range, k = 30), sp = 10e-6, data = train_df)

make a plot

train_df |> 
  add_predictions(wiggly_mod) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = range, y = logratio)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line(aes(y = pred), color = "red")

do a model comparison!

rmse(linear_mod, test_df)
## [1] 0.120459
rmse(smooth_mod, test_df)
## [1] 0.05621946
rmse(wiggly_mod, test_df)
## [1] 0.05880925

Repeat a bunch of times

Use some nice tools

cv_df = 
  crossv_mc(lidar_df, 100)

cv_df |>  pull(train) |> nth(3) |> as_tibble()
## # A tibble: 176 × 3
##       id range logratio
##    <int> <dbl>    <dbl>
##  1     1   390  -0.0504
##  2     2   391  -0.0601
##  3     3   393  -0.0419
##  4     4   394  -0.0510
##  5     6   397  -0.0284
##  6     8   400  -0.0399
##  7    10   403  -0.0395
##  8    11   405  -0.0476
##  9    12   406  -0.0604
## 10    14   409  -0.0382
## # ℹ 166 more rows
cv_df = 
  crossv_mc(lidar_df, 100) |> 
  mutate(
    train = map(train, as_tibble),
    test = map(test, as_tibble)
  )

let’s fit models and get rmses for these.

rmse_comp = function(model, dataset) {
  
  rmse(model, dataset)
  
}
cv_df = 
  cv_df |> 
  mutate(
    linear_fit = map(train, \(df) lm(logratio ~ range, data = df)),
    smooth_fit = map(train, \(df) gam(logratio ~ s(range), data = df)),
    wiggly_fit = map(train, \(df) gam(logratio ~ s(range, k = 30), sp = 10e-6, data = df))
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    rmse_linear = map2_dbl(linear_fit, test, rmse),
    rmse_smooth = map2_dbl(smooth_fit, test, rmse),
    rmse_wiggly = map2_dbl(wiggly_fit, test, rmse)
  )

Look at this!!

cv_df |> 
  select(starts_with("rmse_")) |> 
  pivot_longer(
    everything(),
    names_to = "model",
    names_prefix = "rmse_",
    values_to = "rmse"
  ) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = model, y = rmse)) + 
  geom_violin()

Child growth

growth_df = 
  read_csv("data/nepalese_children.csv") |> 
  mutate(
    weight_ch7 = (weight > 7) * (weight - 7)
  )
## Rows: 2705 Columns: 5
## ── Column specification ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

growth_df

##  2    57     2   14.9  104.   13.9        7.9

## 10    36     2   11.2   79.8  14.4        4.2
## # ℹ 2,695 more rows
growth_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = weight, y = armc)) + 
  geom_point(alpha = .5)

linear_fit = lm(armc ~ weight, data = growth_df)
pwl_fit    = lm(armc ~ weight + weight_ch7, data = growth_df)
smooth_fit = gam(armc ~ s(weight), data = growth_df)
growth_df |> 
  add_predictions(pwl_fit) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = weight, y = armc)) + 
  geom_point(alpha = .5) + 
  geom_line(aes(y = pred), color = "red")

do all the CV stuff we know and love

cv_df = 
  crossv_mc(growth_df, 100) |> 
  mutate(
    train = map(train, as_tibble),
    test = map(test, as_tibble)
  )

here i’m fitting models and getting rmses

cv_df = 
  cv_df |> 
  mutate(
    linear_fit = map(train, \(df) lm(armc ~ weight, data = df)),
    pwl_fit    = map(train, \(df) lm(armc ~ weight + weight_ch7, data = df)),
    smooth_fit = map(train, \(df) gam(armc ~ s(weight), data = df))
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    rmse_linear = map2_dbl(linear_fit, test, rmse),
    rmse_pwl    = map2_dbl(pwl_fit, test, rmse),
    rmse_smooth = map2_dbl(smooth_fit, test, rmse)
  )

Look at this!!

cv_df |> 
  select(starts_with("rmse_")) |> 
  pivot_longer(
    everything(),
    names_to = "model",
    names_prefix = "rmse_",
    values_to = "rmse"
  ) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = model, y = rmse)) + 
  geom_violin()
